hypothesis: Replacing one oldest exact hidden-memory slot with a decoder-built half-life-one-segment EMA of each evicted 64-state segment saves at least 800 actual bytes on the exact 65536-symbol NNCP construction without additional parameters or resident memory.
interfaces_exposed: Completed per-layer NNCP hidden states -> one decoder-built EMA summary in the oldest memory slot -> unchanged attention and arithmetic alphabet.
kill_condition: Retire the one-slot decay-0.5 evicted-segment summary without decay, slot-count, pooling, or context-length sweeps if actual gain is below 800 bytes, any ideal third is nonpositive, exact identity fails, memory fails, or source exceeds 65536 bytes.
promotion_condition: Two encoders and one decoder reproduce exact symbols and identical candidate state; the candidate archive is at least 800 bytes smaller than the faithful 96142-byte NNCP archive, every chronological third has positive aligned ideal branch gain, allocated and reserved memory remain below decimal 10GB, and compressed source is at most 65536 bytes.
retired_neighborhoods: Distinct from longer-memory parameter sweeps and symbol PPM: it replaces one existing hidden state with a recurrent compressed summary, adds no parameter, and holds the 256-slot memory allocation fixed.
title: NNCP evicted-segment EMA memory summary
